subject: french

moments.title: Academie francaise founded
moments.body:
Richelieu gives letters patent on 29 January 1635 to formalise an academy that will regulate the French language.

The Academie has 40 'immortels'.
moments.takeaway: Language policy was instituted as a state project under absolutism.

moments.title: First Dictionnaire de l'Academie
moments.body: The first edition appears after sixty years of work. Successive editions follow into the 20th century; the ninth edition was completed in 2024.
moments.takeaway: Codification of standard French is a multi-century institutional process.

moments.title: Gregoire's report on patois
moments.body: Gregoire reports that fewer than half of French citizens speak standard French. The Revolution begins linking language standardisation to national identity.
moments.takeaway: Revolutionary politics turned linguistic uniformity into a republican project.

now.title: French today
now.body: OIF estimates around 320 million French speakers worldwide, with sharply rising figures projected for francophone Africa. Loi Toubon (1994) regulates language in commercial and official contexts.
now.open_questions: How will French evolve as its demographic centre shifts? How will the Academie respond to inclusive writing and other reforms?

reflection: French illustrates how strongly state institutions can shape the trajectory of a language over centuries.
